content: 1. The solubility of crizotinib may be reduced, leading to decreased bioavailability, although no formal studies have been conducted to confirm this interaction. 2. Cyclosporine and dexlansoprazole may increase each other's toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can cause hypomagnesemia, and this risk is heightened when combined with other drugs that have similar effects. 3. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract pH, such as PPIs, H2-blockers, and antacids, may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 4. Reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs decreases the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, although the area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam (both buccal and intranasal forms) by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may slow diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Both dichlorphenamide and dexlansoprazole decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Dexlansoprazole increases digoxin toxicity risk due to prolonged PPI use, which may cause hypomagnesemia. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Elagolix increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor and a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 9. Eslcarbazepine acetate increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Fedratinib increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Fexinidazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Dexlansoprazole increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of flibanserin adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Dexlansoprazole decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Fosphenytoin decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Dexlansoprazole decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration with PPIs should be avoided if possible. If PPI treatment is required, separate gefitinib and PPI doses by 12 hours. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Dexlansoprazole increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Istradefylline increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 20. Dexlansoprazole decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases. PPIs at doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Dexlansoprazole increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 22. Lenacapavir increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and has the potential to induce or inhibit P-glycoprotein. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Dexlansoprazole increases methotrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity with higher doses. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Dexlansoprazole decreases methylphenidate effects by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. The pH-dependent characteristics of methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) may be altered by co-administration with antacids or acid suppressants. Consider separating the administration of antacids and methylphenidate extended-release capsules. 26. Dexlansoprazole increases midazolam intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase midazolam systemic exposure, prolonging sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Mitotane decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Dexlansoprazole decreases mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The potential interaction applies to mycophenolate mofetil, while enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulations are less sensitive. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Phenytoin decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Dexlansoprazole decreases polysaccharide iron levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Dexlansoprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH, while posaconazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Primidone decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Rifampin decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Ritonavir increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Dexlansoprazole decreases rose hips levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Sparsentan decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Sparsentan, a CYP2C19 inducer, reduces the exposure and efficacy of CYP2C19 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. St. John’s Wort decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Stiripentol decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 39. Dexlansoprazole increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Concomitant administration may increase tacrolimus whole blood concentrations, particularly in intermediate or poor CYP2C19 metabolizers. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Tazemetostat decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexlansoprazole increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Tecovirimat increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP2C8 and CYP2C19 inhibitor and a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Dexlansoprazole increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Triclabendazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole treatment, recheck plasma concentrations after discontinuation of triclabendazole. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Dexlansoprazole decreases vismodegib levels by altering its solubility and reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Voriconazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Acetazolamide increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Anastrozole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Dexlansoprazole decreases axitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Blessed thistle decreases dexlansoprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and its clinical significance is unknown. 50. Dexlansoprazole decreases cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Cyclophosphamide increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 52. Danazol increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Devil’s claw decreases dexlansoprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Drospirenone increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Based on drug interaction studies with the components of Stribild, no clinically significant interactions are expected when co-administered with PPIs. 56. Dexlansoprazole decreases ferric carboxymaltose levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Larotrectinib increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Levoketoconazole increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Dexlansoprazole decreases levothyroxine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction.
